assessed_by: mined-row fields; traversal attempted and not needed

discovery.found_by: the 10 production adaptations the census listed under 'Unchecked leads (traversal NEVER run)'

scope: All 10 production-adaptation rows: toscollection/tcommon-studio-se, opensearch-project/OpenSearch, anubhavg-icpl/opensearch (a fork of the former), finos/fluxnova-bpm-platform x4, camunda/camunda x2, wiremock/wiremock. Roughly 5 distinct projects once forks and repeated crossings are collapsed.

why_excluded.finding: Every row fails two necessary conditions independently, so no traversal verdict could change the outcome.
why_excluded.reason_1_not_declared_directly: version_at_commit and version_at_parent are None for all 10 rows: json-smart is not declared in any of these projects' build files. It arrives transitively (commonly via nimbus-jose-jwt). The study covers direct-dependency bumps only.
why_excluded.reason_2_no_library_code_changed: library_referenced_files is EMPTY for all 10. Not one changed production file references json-smart, so there is no library-using code that could have been adapted.
why_excluded.traversal_evidence: Traversal was run on the three that completed within 240s (tcommon-studio-se, both opensearch rows) and returned `resolution: unresolved` -- BOM/parent-managed, undecided -- for each. The remaining seven timed out on very large monorepos. Under the direct-only scoping rule, unresolved/transitive is out of scope, so the timeouts change nothing.
why_excluded.consistency_with_the_break: This matches what the README already records for json-smart under screening rule 4: it is used transitively, 89% of mined commits changed no Java, so nobody has code against it to adapt.

process_note: The census listed these as 'work not done rather than a measured negative', and running traversal was the obvious response. It was unnecessary -- the disposing evidence (null declared version, empty library_referenced_files) was already in the candidate rows. Check the mined fields before spending traversal time on large repositories.
